newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES hopes for $500m World Bank loan.
newsitem.headline: UES hopes for $500m World Bank loan.

text.p: Unified Energy System (UES), Russia's national electricity generator, said on Thursday it hoped to receive a $500 million loan from the World Bank to build a power station in southern Russia.

"Together with World Bank experts, we have done a huge amount of work...Now, after five years of talks, we have prospects of receiving the loan," Anatoly Dyakov, President of RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES), told a news conference.
"We hope now the bank will not go back on its promises and will finance us," said Dyakov. He declined to say when he expected the credit.
Dyakov said UES had agreed with the World Bank that the Kuban power station in the Krasnodar region, with a capacity of 900,000 kilowatts, would be a separate legal entity.
He said UES also agreed to hold a tender for foreign companies to supply the future station with necessary equipment once the credit agreement has been signed.

The World Bank does not lend directly to companies, only to governments, which on-lend to companies. A World Bank spokeswoman in Moscow confirmed the bank was discussing a power-generation project with the government, but said it was too soon to give details.
UES owns Russia's Russia's electricity grid and has 49-100 percent stakes in 68 out of 71 local power companies. --Dmitry Solovyov, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
